text: Vouch Chain Impl v3 WeB0nd MVP: The “Vouch Chain” with Introductions and City- Aware Discovery (T3 Stack / Prisma Edition) Core Concept Membership is invitation-only: trusted users vouch by sharing invite links, creating scarcity, desire, and a seeded social graph from day one. In addition to direct vouches, the system supports mediated introductions—if A vouched for B and B vouched for C, then A can request B to introduce them to C. All of this is surfaced with geographic awareness: users can set and validate their city, and discovery (including vouch chains and introduction paths) can be filtered or prioritized by city. Validation & Success Metrics • Viral Coefficient: Number of new members each seed member generates. • Conversion Rate: Percentage of invite link clicks that become signups. • Engagement: Share of users who both vouch and act on introductions. • Introduction Flow Metrics: – Requests initiated (e.g., A asking B to introduce to C) – Approvals/completions (intermediary facilitating the intro) – Conversion from introductions to meaningful connections – Geographic breakdown (same-city vs cross-city introductions) • Geographic Discovery Usage: Frequency and effectiveness of city-based filtering in connection paths. • Qualitative Feedback: Perceived value of exclusivity, mediated intro- ductions, and local relevance from user interviews. 1 Phase 1: Foundation & Core MVP Logic (Days 1–4) Data Modeling & Schema • Define a canonical, strongly-typed data schema in Prisma including: – User with fields for identity, invite code, vouch relationships (who vouched them and whom they vouched), vouch count, and normal- ized/validated city. – IntroductionRequest capturing requester, intermediary, target, status (requested, approved, completed, declined), timestamps, and optional contextual messages. – City metadata (city name, region/state, country, and optional geolocation) stored in normalized form to support consistent filtering and discovery. Authentication • Use NextAuth.js with the Google provider for primary login. • Integrate the Prisma adapter to automatically manage and persist user records upon signup. Vouching & Introduction Logic • Implement vouching flow: users join via invite links, get linked to their voucher, and vouch counts are updated. • Implement mediated introductions: – Logic to discover valid introduction chains (e.g., A → B → C). – Flow for A to request B to introduce to C. – State management for introduction requests (request, approve/reject, complete). – Optional message/context on approval to enrich the handoff. City Validation & Profile Updates • Add a normalized, validated city field to user profiles. • Provide autocomplete-driven input for cities (backed by a reliable source or internal curated list) to ensure consistent city names and support fuzzy matching with fallback. • Allow users to update their city with real-time validation feedback; support admin override for edge cases. • Store both the raw input and normalized representation to support analytics and auditing. 2 Geographic Discovery • Enable filtering of vouch chains and potential introductions based on city (e.g., show connections within Miami or surface multi-hop intro paths crossing cities). • Surface geographically relevant suggestions when users explore their net- work. Phase 2: Frontend Development & Deployment (Days 5–8) UI & UX Components • Vouch Landing Page: Invite acceptance flow prompting Google sign-in and linking into the vouch network. • Onboarding Flow: Collect phone number, optional Instagram handle, and validated city as part of initial profile completion. • Introduction Workflow Interfaces: – Discovery UI for identifying potential targets (C) via eligible interme- diaries (B). – Request submission UI for A to ask B for an intro. – Dashboard for intermediaries to review, approve/reject, and facilitate introductions with optional context. – Notification system for all parties (request sent, approved/denied, intro completed). • City Picker/Profile Editor: Autocomplete-enabled city selection with validation, current city display, and edit capability. • Social Graph / Ledger Visualization: Geographic filters, highlighting local clusters, and overlaying introduction opportunities on the vouch chain. Deployment • Deploy the full application to Vercel. • Connect the GitHub repository, configure environment variables including database URL, Twilio credentials, analytics keys, and any external city- validation service keys. • Ensure migrations and build steps integrate seamlessly into Vercel’s pipeline. 3 Phase 3: Instagram Verification & Analytics (Days 9–11) Instagram Verification • Implement a manual verification flow for Instagram handles: – User submits their handle, sees a unique code, and is instructed to send it via DM to a controlled admin account. – Admin interface lists pending verifications; admins confirm the code and mark handles as VERIFIED. • Support lightweight profile photo retrieval from public Instagram endpoints as a temporary MVP approach (with explicit acknowledgment of its fragility and potential future breakage). Analytics Integration • Integrate PostHog to capture both client-side and server-side events, including: – vouch_requested – vouch_accepted – invite_sent – intro_request_sent – intro_request_approved – intro_completed • Enrich analytics events with city metadata to track geographic patterns in adoption, introduction flows, and engagement. Phase 4: Testing, Monitoring & Iteration (Days 12–14) Testing • Validate core flows: authentication, vouching, introduction request lifecycle, and city validation/update. • Exercise edge cases: broken chains, stale intermediaries, ambiguous city inputs, and rejected introduction paths. Monitoring • Track the health and performance of the introduction subsystem (e.g., failure rates, latency, stale pending requests). • Monitor geographic distribution and growth trends to identify strong local clusters or underpenetrated cities. • Use PostHog to observe funnel conversion for both vouches and introduc- tions. 4 Iteration • Refine introduction path suggestions based on response rates, geography, and historical conversion performance. • Improve city autocomplete accuracy and expand fallback handling for ambiguous entries. • Test and optimize incentives or UX tweaks to increase completion of introductions and correct city tagging. Strategic Benefits • Unified Stack: T3 Stack with Prisma and tRPC consolidates the data, logic, and deployment layers into a cohesive, type-safe development experi- ence that reduces friction and accelerates iterations. • Amplified Network Effects: Mediated introductions extend reach be- yond direct vouches, enabling warm connections that carry more implicit trust. • Local Relevance: City-aware discovery and normalized location data help surface connections that are contextually meaningful, improving utility and retention. • Richer Signals: Combining vouch chains, introductions, and geographic metadata yields deeper behavioral insights for personalization, seeding strategy, and growth optimization. 5
